title: Crypto audit streamliner: automated KMS/HSM evidence exports and verifiable key-rotation trails
creator: Amina Patel
description: Objective: Build an automated, auditable pipeline that produces tamper-evident encryption evidence artifacts for KMS/HSM integrations, key rotation events, and data residency/retention compliance. This work will cover both platform-managed and customer-managed keys across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
background: Customers and auditors are requesting machine-readable evidence that: (a) keys used to encrypt customer data are rotated on a predictable cadence, (b) key provenance and KMS/HSM attestation are recorded, and (c) evidence artifacts are immutable, signed, and retained according to retention policies. Current artifacts are ad-hoc (logs + screenshots) and require manual gathering.
goals: Produce a signed artifact for each key rotation event containing key alias, KMS provider, key metadata, rotation timestamp, rotation reason, and a cryptographic signature from a dedicated attestation key
Expose an evidence export API and one-click report in Console for a date range and per-customer scope
Store artifacts with immutability controls (object lock / WORM) and retention metadata per customer residency settings
Automate monthly and on-demand audit bundles with checksum and manifest file linking to rotation + encryption configuration snapshots
constraints_and_tradeoffs: Attestation key must be protected in HSM — limits ability to run end-to-end tests in dev without hardware; we'll provide a simulator key for dev environment

Enforcing object-lock on existing buckets is complex for Dedicated/Private; for those deployments we'll provide a co-located immutable store option (S3 object lock when available, otherwise append-only DB with signed manifests)
Generating signatures for every tokenized event adds ~3-10ms per rotation pipeline step; acceptable for periodic rotations but not per-request operations
We will capture hashed snapshots of KV cache state and model references but will not include raw customer data in artifacts to avoid data leakage
design_decisions: Use envelope encryption model: platform stores data keys encrypted by KMS; rotation events create a new data key and rewrap metadata where necessary
Attestation signatures will use an HSM-resident RSA-3072 key with SHA-256; provide both RSA and ECDSA verification signatures in the manifest for cross-compatibility
Artifacts are JSON-LD manifests (schema v1) including standardized fields: event_id, key_id, kms_provider, region, rotation_time, previous_key_fingerprint, signed_by, signature, evidence_ttl
Retention metadata stored in tenant config and enforced by the export pipeline; deletions should create a deletion-event artifact signed by the attestation key

acceptance_criteria: Given a KMS-managed key rotation, the system writes a signed evidence manifest to the configured immutable store within 60s of the rotation event
Manifests validate with the provided HSM public key and include all required fields from schema v1
Console export returns a zipped audit bundle containing manifests, signed deletion events (if applied), and a top-level checksum manifest
Retention rules cause artifacts to be deleted only after a signed deletion-event is produced and retention window expires; automated deletion events are captured in the audit stream
E2E test exists that verifies signature verification for AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HashiCorp Vault simulated HSM

notes_for_oncall: If attestation signing fails (HSM timeout or PKCS#11 error), pipeline should mark artifact state as 'signing-failed' and emit alert to sec-ops channel. For Dedicated/Private where HSM is customer-managed, fall back to storing unsigned manifest with a signed-notice explaining the reason.
